title: objectql: a manifest objectExtensions entry or hydrated row whose extend folds to a legacy key opens a second, owner-less object entry
body:
domain:server#1 · os-project-manager · session_01R1q2xdtYgU6FKrZ7LgjPCC

Filing gate: ① should-fix of the PR #28853 contract review (card #28834), out of that PR's surface by its claim. Carried to its own card by this seat. Filed by `domain:server` seat 1. ⛔ Not a claim. Graded by this seat p3 under 「定级你可以自己决定」 (Leehom, 2026-11-01): it reaches only a legacy `ns__name` object key, and no shipped manifest reaches it (measured on #28834).

Reach: a code package whose manifest `objectExtensions[]` names a short `extend` that `getObject` folds to a legacy `ns__name` key, and a stored `object_extension` row with such a spelling at boot hydration.

## What happens (read by the review at PR #28853's head `461552ac`)

PR #28853 makes the `object_extension` item gate refuse an `extend` that `getObject` resolves to a different key. Two other entries still file `extend` verbatim:
- the manifest `objectExtensions` loop in `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` (about L9455);
- the at-rest hydration of a stored row.

`registerObjectExtension` then calls `registerObject` with `computeFQN` as the identity. That opens an owner-less entry under the short name, beside the real object, and nothing checks it (`assertSingleOwnerPerObject` has no source caller).

## Wanted

One answer at every entry: an `extend` that `getObject` folds to a different key never opens a second entry. Either refuse it with the item gate's sentence, or report it at the fold the way the registry reports a field-patch miss. The route is the dispatching seat's call. Measure first: count stored rows and manifests in the repo and in hotcrm, and say whether a legacy key is still reachable at all.

Dedupe: searched `extend getObject fold legacy key manifest objectExtensions`. Related: #28834 (the item door half, PR #28853). **New.**

Links back: #28834, PR #28853, #28574, ADR-0146 D10.
